title: cairn site settings
description: Site chrome: title, languages, welcome note, links, hosted pages, status. Docs: https://github.com/MorganKryze/cairn/blob/main/docs/configuration/site.md

title.description: The site name, shown in the header and the tab. Plain text or a per-locale mapping.

tagline.description: One sentence describing the site, translatable.

url.description: Public base URL (https://…). Enables canonical links, hreflang and an absolute sitemap.

logo.description: Image shown before the title: URL or /assets path, or the pair {light, dark} when one image cannot serve both themes. A raster logo also becomes the social preview image when url is set; that preview has no theme, so it is always the light one.

oneOf.description: Two images, keyed by the theme each one appears in. Both are required: half a pair paints nothing in one theme. e.g. {light: /assets/logo.svg, dark: /assets/logo-white.svg}

dark.description: Shown in the dark theme. A monochrome mark needs this: on cairn's tile a black one reads 1.40:1 against the dark theme, where the rules ask 3:1.

favicon.description: Tab icon: URL or /assets path, or the pair {light, dark}. Defaults to cairn's own, which is drawn to read on both. The dark one follows the visitor's system and the theme button; the web app manifest has no theme, so it always takes the light one.

oneOf.description: Two images, keyed by the theme each one appears in. Both are required: half a pair paints nothing in one theme. e.g. {light: /assets/fav.svg, dark: /assets/fav-white.svg}

dark.description: Shown in the dark theme. A monochrome mark needs this: on cairn's tile a black one reads 1.40:1 against the dark theme, where the rules ask 3:1.

icons.description: Home-screen icons, for "add to home screen" and the browser install prompt. Supply them yourself when you want the full set: cairn never resizes an image. Omit this and the icons are derived from favicon, or are cairn's own.

src.description: URL or /assets path to the image.

sizes.description: Its real size, like "512x512", or "any" for an svg. Chromium offers to install a site only when a 192 and a 512 are both present.

purpose.description: any, maskable or monochrome; they may be combined, as in "any maskable". A maskable icon must keep its content inside the middle 80%, because Android crops the rest.

index.description: false asks search engines to stay away: robots.txt disallows, pages carry noindex, the sitemap turns off.

locales.description: Enabled languages; the first is the default. Codes like fr, en, pt-BR.

accent.description: The accent color, a hex value like "#247b7b".

font.description: The dashboard's body font. family is a CSS font stack; file is a font in the config directory's fonts/ folder, served by cairn itself so the page makes no external font request.

family.description: CSS font-family list for body text, e.g. "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif". When file is set, the first name in the list is the one the file provides.

file.description: A woff2, woff, ttf or otf file inside the config directory's fonts/ folder (e.g. fonts/custom-font.woff2), served by cairn itself, no external request. Requires family to name it.

about.description: Dismissable welcome note on the home page, translatable. Long text: paragraphs and CommonMark, minus raw HTML.

icon.description: A built-in glyph (book, chat, github, globe, heart, home, key, mail, portfolio, rss, status, user), a URL, or an /assets path.

footer.description: Footer links, before the hosted pages.

pages.description: Pages cairn serves itself (legal notice, privacy…), linked in the footer.

body.description: Intro text. Long text: paragraphs and CommonMark, minus raw HTML. The page title is the h1, so start headings here at ##.

credit.description: false removes the footer "powered by cairn".

show_version.description: true prints the running cairn version beside the credit: the release number for a tagged build, the commit for a build off main. Off by default.

strings.description: Overrides for built-in UI strings, keyed like search.placeholder.

contact.description: Where to report a vulnerability, as a URI: mailto:security@example.org, https://example.org/report, tel:+33.... Setting it is what makes cairn serve /.well-known/security.txt.

policy.description: URL of your disclosure policy, if you publish one.

encryption.description: URL of the public key a reporter should encrypt to.

hosting_flag.description: Where the self-hosted and external flags on a card lead. Each value is the id of a page cairn serves, an absolute path, or a URL; a page id resolves in the language the visitor is reading. Leave one out and that flag stays plain text.

self.description: Where the Self-hosted flag leads: a page id, an absolute path, or a URL.

external.description: Where the External flag leads: a page id, an absolute path, or a URL.

service_links.description: How the two links that lead to a service behave: the name on a card, and the button on a detail page. Only links that leave the site are affected; a service whose url is a page cairn serves is untouched. Both keys are off by default.

new_tab.description: true opens a service link in a new tab, with rel="noopener noreferrer", so the directory stays where the visitor left it. Off by default.

confirm.description: Which service links raise a dialog naming the destination before the visitor follows them. "external" covers only the services flagged selfhosted: false, which is the case worth a sentence; "all" covers every link that leaves the site, and true means the same. Off by default. A service with no selfhosted flag never counts as external.

gatus.description: Gatus base URL cairn polls for the status pills. The same address can be written as status.url with status.provider: gatus.

provider.description: Which monitor answers at status.url. status.gatus names its own, so a site polling Gatus needs neither key.

url.description: Address of the monitor named by status.provider. The generic spelling of status.gatus: set one or the other, never both.

slug.description: Uptime Kuma only: the published status page cairn reads, named by the last part of its URL (https://kuma.example.org/status/tools -> tools). Kuma serves statuses per status page, so this is half the address.

map.description: status.provider: json only: how to read somebody else's status document. A path is a dotted walk and nothing more.

list.description: Path to the array of services. Empty when the document is itself the array.

key.description: Field of each element holding the service name, which has to match a cairn service id for a pill to be drawn.

state.description: Field of each element holding its state.

up.description: Values that mean up. An allow-list: a state in none of the three lists reads as down.

degraded.description: Values that mean it works, but not well.

maintenance.description: Values that mean off on purpose.

unknown.description: Values that mean nobody is checking, such as a paused monitor. Those services get no pill at all rather than a red one.

token_file.description: Absolute path of a file holding the bearer token for the status API, never the token itself. A kubernetes secret, a docker secret and a vault agent all deliver one. It may not be under /assets, which cairn serves to every visitor.

token_scheme.description: Authorization scheme sent with the token; Bearer by default, OAuth for Atlassian Statuspage.

page.description: Public Gatus URL the pills link to; set it when the poll URL is internal.

interval.description: Poll cadence, a duration of at least 5s (e.g. 60s). Also how often a page already open in a browser refreshes its pills.

insecure.description: true stops cairn verifying the certificate Gatus presents, for an internal Gatus whose authority nothing public signed. A CA bundle verifies instead of trusting; this only turns the check off. cairn logs it at startup and cairn -check warns about it every run.

ca.description: PEM bundle cairn verifies Gatus against, on top of the system roots: an http(s):// URL it fetches once, or an /assets path it reads. The answer status.insecure is not, and the opposite one: this verifies rather than stops checking. Fetched over http it lands where insecure does, so cairn says which of the two it is at startup and on every -check.

linked.description: false makes the pills display-only: they still show up, down or unknown, but they stop linking to the status page. For a Gatus your visitors cannot reach.
